# Azure Monitor Generated OpenTelemetry Exporter Client

> see <https://aka.ms/autorest>

## Instructions

From `swagger/`:

```zsh
rm -rf ../src/generated
autorest swagger/README.md
```

## Configuration

```yaml
package-name: "@azure/monitor-opentelemetry-exporter"
title: ApplicationInsightsClient
description: Application Insights Client
generate-metadata: false
license-header: MICROSOFT_MIT_NO_VERSION
output-folder: ../
source-code-folder-path: ./src/generated
input-file: https://github.com/Azure/azure-rest-api-specs/blob/main/specification/applicationinsights/data-plane/Monitor.Exporters/preview/v2.1/swagger.json
add-credentials: false
use-extension:
  "@autorest/typescript": "6.0.34"
package-version: 1.0.0-beta.25
typescript: true
v3: true
module-kind: esm
```

proposals.subtype: Construct an observable customer-SDK metrics provider
proposals.explanation: The constructor creates a periodic reader, meter provider, named meter and three observable gauges, initializes counters/dimensions and starts asynchronous initialization without awaiting it. Its interval is networkCollectionInterval or a 900000 ms fallback using truthiness, not validation; language/version/attach values come from imported helpers/constants.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This exporter-side OpenTelemetry integration imports generated envelope types from a separate generated module; the supplied generator configuration places protocol output in src/generated.

proposals.subtype: Create a metrics singleton after a dynamically imported exporter
proposals.explanation: getInstance checks the static instance before and after awaiting a dynamic exporter import, constructs an instrumentation-key/endpoint connection string and creates the exporter and metrics instance only inside the second check. Later calls return the existing instance rather than replacing its options.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured exporter integration implements its own asynchronous instance coordination outside the declared generated protocol tree.

proposals.subtype: Shut down a metrics provider and clear its matching singleton
proposals.explanation: The static shutdown forwards when an instance exists; the instance method awaits meter-provider shutdown and clears the singleton only when it still refers to this instance. A rejected provider shutdown bypasses the subsequent clearing statement.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: These lifecycle methods belong to the captured exporter-side metrics class, not the generated ingestion client.

proposals.subtype: Register metric callbacks after resource-provider initialization
proposals.explanation: initialize awaits the base resource-provider helper, then registers bound success, drop and retry batch callbacks against their gauges. A caught failure emits a debug message and is not rethrown; the base helper's behavior is unavailable.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-protocol exporter integration explicitly coordinates resource discovery and OpenTelemetry callback registration.

proposals.subtype: Observe and reset positive successful-item counters
proposals.explanation: itemSuccessCallback observes positive counts with customer properties and telemetry type, then resets only those positive entries to zero. It does not clear the map or reset nonpositive entries.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This is explicit exporter-side counter observation over generated-envelope-derived statistics, outside protocol generation.

proposals.subtype: Observe dropped-item dimensions and reset every visited count
proposals.explanation: itemDropCallback traverses type/code/reason/success maps, adds a truthy reason and a non-null success dimension only for request/dependency telemetry, and observes positive counts. It resets every visited count, including nonpositive entries, without clearing the map structure.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The exporter integration implements the nested aggregation-to-gauge projection itself, separate from generated ingestion models.

proposals.subtype: Observe retry dimensions and reset every visited count
proposals.explanation: itemRetryCallback traverses type/code/reason maps, conditionally adds a reason attribute, observes only positive counts and resets all visited counts to zero. It emits measurements rather than executing retries.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured exporter integration explicitly implements this retry-statistics projection outside generated protocol output.

proposals.subtype: Count successful envelopes by their classified telemetry type
proposals.explanation: countSuccessfulItems classifies each supplied envelope and increments its type's map entry from the existing value or zero. The body does not determine whether an upload actually succeeded.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The exporter integration implements aggregation over imported generated envelope types, not generated REST behavior.

proposals.subtype: Count drops by telemetry type, code, reason and conditional success
proposals.explanation: countDroppedItems creates nested maps as needed, derives a reason, and increments one entry per supplied envelope. Request/dependency success is used when defined; other cases use a null success key. This records caller-reported drops rather than making drop decisions.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured exporter-specific class implements its own nested aggregation around generated envelope models.

proposals.subtype: Map reported drop codes into diagnostic reason labels
proposals.explanation: getDropReason prioritizes a truthy explicit exception type for CLIENT_EXCEPTION, otherwise classifies an available message or uses the fallback exception label. Numeric codes use the status classifier; other code branches select readonly, persistence-capacity, storage-disabled or unknown reason members. It does not implement those error conditions.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The exporter-side helper contains explicit diagnostic mapping branches outside generated transport/model code.

proposals.subtype: Classify diagnostic messages by ordered substring heuristics
proposals.explanation: categorizeExceptionMessage lowercases text, tests timeout phrases first, then network/connection/DNS/socket terms, then disk/storage/file/persist terms, and otherwise returns the client-exception label. These substring labels do not prove the underlying cause or actual exception type.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The exporter integration implements this concrete diagnostic heuristic rather than relying on a generated error model.

proposals.subtype: Describe status codes for diagnostic statistics
proposals.explanation: categorizeStatusCode supplies named descriptions for selected 4xx/5xx values, range fallbacks for other values in those ranges and status_<value> otherwise. It neither changes retryability nor guarantees a fixed-size set of labels for arbitrary numeric input.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured exporter helper implements the status-to-label switch separately from generated HTTP response handling.

proposals.subtype: Count reported retry envelopes by telemetry type, code and reason
proposals.explanation: countRetryItems creates nested type/code/reason maps and increments one entry for each envelope using the derived retry reason. This method counts reported attempts and performs no retry, delay or request dispatch.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The exporter-specific class implements its own retry-statistics aggregation around generated envelope types.

proposals.subtype: Map reported retry codes to diagnostic reason labels
proposals.explanation: getRetryReason applies explicit-type/message/fallback precedence for CLIENT_EXCEPTION, delegates numeric codes to status labeling and maps CLIENT_TIMEOUT or unknown cases to imported reason members. It reports reasons without controlling request retry policy.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This exporter integration explicitly implements the retry-label selection branches outside generated protocol output.

proposals.subtype: Classify envelopes and distinguish performance-counter metrics
proposals.explanation: getTelemetryTypeFromEnvelope maps known baseType strings to telemetry types and returns UNKNOWN for absent/unrecognized values. MetricData becomes PERFORMANCE_COUNTER when any metric name belongs to Object.values(BreezePerformanceCounterNames), otherwise CUSTOM_METRIC; the actual imported name set is not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The exporter integration explicitly interprets imported generated envelope data and applies an additional metric-name classification.

proposals.subtype: Extract a success field only for request/dependency envelopes
proposals.explanation: getTelemetrySuccessFromEnvelope returns baseData.success for RequestData or RemoteDependencyData and undefined when data is missing or the type differs. Type assertions do not validate or coerce the returned field at runtime.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This exporter-side helper projects a diagnostic dimension from generated envelope model types.

proposals.subtype: Recognize timeout-like codes or diagnostic message phrases
proposals.explanation: isTimeoutError accepts four exact error-code strings or a lowercase message containing timeout, timed out or connection reset, otherwise returning false. Its heuristic includes connection-reset/DNS codes and does not establish an actual timeout or trigger a retry; callers are not supplied.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The exporter integration implements the concrete error-label heuristic rather than importing a generated retry policy.

proposals.subtype: Lazily reuse one customer-stats manager instance
proposals.explanation: CustomerSDKStatsManager.getInstance creates its private-constructor instance only when the static field is absent, then returns that field. This coordinates this module/class instance, not a demonstrated singleton across independent module copies.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied stats integration defines its own stateful manager outside the generated protocol tree.

proposals.subtype: Gate stats activation on configuration and environment-variable truthiness
proposals.explanation: The configuration callback ignores a missing feature key or nonboolean evaluation, otherwise updates the enabled state and queues reconciliation. canStart also requires options and the absence of truthy values for both imported disable-variable names; it does not parse strings such as false as booleans. The remote-enabled field initially defaults true.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This stats manager directly connects the captured configuration system to the exporter-side metrics lifecycle.

proposals.subtype: Retain initial stats options and expose desired-state lifecycle controls
proposals.explanation: initialize keeps a shallow copy of only the first options, registers the configuration callback once, recomputes desired state and queues an update. shutdown clears desired state and queues another update; the getter hides metrics unless desired and not stopping. Shutdown does not unregister the callback or clear options in this body.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured non-protocol manager implements lifecycle/control APIs over the exporter-side metrics resource.

proposals.subtype: Serialize asynchronous stats creation and shutdown transitions
proposals.explanation: update chains applyState on both resolution and rejection of the previous transition. Reconciliation stops unwanted/stopping metrics, creates a missing desired instance and rechecks desired state after creation. stop clears resource/stopping fields only after successful shutdown, so failure can leave the stopping state set for a later attempt.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The stats integration implements the explicit promise queue and resource state machine outside generated REST operations.

proposals.subtype: Lazily reuse a configuration-manager instance
proposals.explanation: ConfigurationManager.getInstance creates the manager only when its static instance is absent. Worker/callback/cache state therefore belongs to that reused instance in the current module context.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This is explicit state coordination in the supplied SDK configuration integration, outside declared protocol generation.

proposals.subtype: Fill a configuration profile and start at most one polling worker
proposals.explanation: initialize merges caller profile values with a truthy Microsoft-distro version in preference to an Azure-Monitor-distro version, then invokes the write-once profile fill even if a worker already exists. Only an absent worker is constructed with the refresh method as callback; environment values win this merge, not previously populated profile fields.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured configuration integration explicitly composes the supplied profile and polling-worker classes.

proposals.subtype: Stop the configuration worker and release callback subscriptions
proposals.explanation: shutdown calls the worker's shutdown when present, clears the worker reference and empties the callback list. It does not itself reset cached settings, ETag, backoff attempts or the profile.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-protocol configuration manager explicitly manages its worker and callback lifecycle.

proposals.subtype: Register independently removable callbacks with cached-state replay
proposals.explanation: registerCallback wraps each registration, immediately invokes it when cached settings have at least one key, and returns a closure removing that wrapper. Repeated registrations of the same original callback remain independently removable; replay is not awaited here.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured SDK configuration integration implements callback subscription and cached replay rather than a generated service operation.

proposals.subtype: Dispatch callback snapshots while logging synchronous and asynchronous failures
proposals.explanation: notifyCallbacks iterates a copied subscription array. invokeCallback catches synchronous throws and attaches a rejection handler through Promise.resolve, logging either failure without awaiting callbacks or rethrowing it. This isolates invocation failures, not nested settings mutation.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The non-protocol configuration integration implements explicit callback error handling and dispatch.

proposals.subtype: Perform conditional change detection, backoff and settings refresh
proposals.explanation: The refresh method sends interval/optional ETag headers, returns capped exponential backoff for transient change responses, handles 304 by retaining settings and updating metadata, and uses a second request after 200. Failed/empty configuration fetches retain settings without advancing the ETag; successful nonempty fetches shallow-freeze a copied settings object and notify callbacks. Abort checks preserve current cadence, other change statuses return the maximum interval, and imported helper/constant implementations are absent.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured configuration integration implements the two-stage conditional-request state machine and error classification outside generated ingestion operations.

proposals.subtype: Return a shallow copy of cached settings
proposals.explanation: getSettings returns a new top-level object spread from cached settings. Its Readonly return type does not freeze this returned object or clone nested values.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The SDK configuration integration explicitly exposes a cache snapshot rather than a generated response model.

proposals.subtype: Reset configuration state and backoff after shutdown
proposals.explanation: reset shuts down the worker/subscriptions, recreates state with the imported default refresh interval and empty settings, and clears the backoff counter. It does not replace the static manager instance or reset the separate profile.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This executable reset belongs to the supplied configuration integration rather than a test file or generated REST operation.

proposals.subtype: Lazily reuse a configuration-profile instance
proposals.explanation: ConfigurationProfile.getInstance lazily constructs and returns a static profile instance initialized with empty-string fields. Reuse is scoped to this class/module context.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied configuration system defines this shared profile separately from generated protocol models.

proposals.subtype: Fill only still-empty known profile fields
proposals.explanation: fill iterates the existing field names and assigns an incoming non-undefined value only when the stored value is an empty string. Existing nonempty values and omitted fields remain unchanged; assigning another empty string leaves the field eligible for later filling.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The captured configuration integration implements an explicit state-merge rule consumed by the supplied configuration manager.

proposals.subtype: Return a shallow copy of current profile values
proposals.explanation: snapshot returns an object spread of the current profile, typed Readonly but without a runtime freeze. The declared profile fields are strings; this method does not mutate stored values.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied configuration profile explicitly implements this snapshot API outside generated protocol models.

proposals.subtype: Reset all profile fields to their empty initial values
proposals.explanation: reset replaces the profile's values object with emptyProfile's seven empty-string fields. It does not replace the singleton or stop a polling worker.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: This executable integration method is in the captured source, not a test or an empty generated-model stub.

proposals.subtype: Schedule nonoverlapping background configuration polls with startup jitter
proposals.explanation: The worker starts with a randomized 5-15 second delay and unrefs its recursive timer. Each loop awaits one poll with a new abort signal, accepts a finite positive interval capped through the imported maximum, logs failures/invalid intervals and retains the prior interval, then reschedules only while running. This is background configuration polling, not an SDK LRO.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The complete configuration integration implements its own timer/abort/poll loop outside generated ingestion operations.

proposals.subtype: Stop future polls and abort the active configuration request
proposals.explanation: shutdown returns early when already stopped, otherwise clears running, aborts the current controller and cancels/clears any pending timer. It requests cancellation but does not await an active poll's completion.
proposals.handwrittenRationale: The supplied configuration integration contains this explicit background-resource cleanup implementation.

decisions.reason: Lines 57-101 construct an OpenTelemetry metric reader/provider, three gauges, and dimensions in exporter integration outside the declared src/generated protocol output. The stated interval and unawaited initialization are visible; generator support is appropriately left unclear.

Lines 109-123 contain both singleton checks around the dynamic import and construct a configured stats exporter. This is a distinct resource-creation behavior in non-protocol integration; a generic asynchronous singleton template is a plausible, not demonstrated, generator feature.
Lines 129-142 show forwarding, provider shutdown, and conditional instance clearing. Resource teardown is distinct from construction, and generic lifecycle generation is plausible, not established.

Lines 149-164 await the inherited resource helper and explicitly register three bound observable callbacks; the superclass implementation is not captured. This callback integration is separate from constructing the provider.
Lines 167-182 observe and zero only positive per-type success counts, a concrete telemetry aggregation-to-gauge behavior.

Lines 184-234 project nested drop counts into conditional diagnostic dimensions and zero every visited leaf, unlike the success callback; the proposal correctly distinguishes recording drops from causing them.
Lines 236-274 observe dimensioned retry counts and reset all leaves. This measures caller-reported retries rather than performing request retries.
Lines 282-292 increment per-envelope, per-type success counts without determining the actual upload outcome; the distinct accumulation behavior is captured.
Lines 301-348 aggregate reported drops by type/code/reason and conditional success, separately from the observation and reset callback.
Lines 357-391 select diagnostic drop labels by explicit type, message, numeric status, or enumerated reason. The mapping does not establish the true cause of a drop.

The substring-based classifier is real and independently reusable, but nothing supplied establishes a TypeSpec or generator mechanism for these chosen diagnostic phrases; generator addressability is unclear rather than yes.

finding.subtype: Classify diagnostic messages by ordered substring heuristics
finding.explanation: The method lowercases messages and checks timeout, network, then storage phrases in order, otherwise returning a generic client-exception label. The labels do not prove the underlying exception type.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The exporter-side stats class implements explicit phrase matching outside the separately declared src/generated protocol output; no generated counterpart is supplied.

decisions.reason: The diagnostic label mapping is supported, but the captured source does not justify treating the specific labels and fallback as plausibly generated from TypeSpec; addressability remains unclear.

finding.subtype: Describe status codes for diagnostic statistics
finding.explanation: The method maps selected HTTP status codes to named diagnostic descriptions, other 4xx/5xx codes to range labels, and all remaining numbers to a status-prefixed string. It does not change request retry policy.
finding.handwrittenRationale: This explicit status-label switch is in exporter-side telemetry integration, rather than the separately declared generated ingestion client.

decisions.reason: Lines 476-508 accumulate retry-statistic dimensions; they do not dispatch or retry a request, and the telemetry category accurately reflects that.
Lines 517-547 choose a diagnostic reason for reported retries; the explanation correctly separates labeling from retry policy.
Lines 554-600 explicitly map envelope baseType values and distinguish MetricData with a performance-counter name. The imported name set is unavailable, as acknowledged.
Lines 607-622 extract a diagnostic success dimension for two envelope base types, with no runtime verification of the asserted model types.
The code-based and phrase-based timeout diagnostic heuristic is captured, but no supplied generator inputs establish it as a plausible TypeSpec-generated behavior; retain unclear addressability.

finding.subtype: Recognize timeout-like codes or diagnostic message phrases
finding.explanation: The method matches four exact error codes or case-insensitive timeout/connection-reset phrases and otherwise returns false. DNS and connection-reset matches do not prove a timeout; no caller or request retry is captured.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The exporter-side telemetry class implements explicit error-label heuristics outside the separately declared generated protocol tree; no generated counterpart is supplied.

decisions.reason: Lines 42-49 only implement lazy instantiation of the stats manager; the behavioral customization is its feature-gated metrics lifecycle in proposals 18-20. Counting this generic object-construction detail as another instance would double-count that integration.

Lines 27-40 and 70-77 independently determine whether telemetry runs based on evaluated settings, options, and truthy disable variables. Missing or invalid feature results leave the current setting unchanged.

Lines 51-68 retain the first options, subscribe once, queue state reconciliation, and restrict exposure of the metrics instance; these lifecycle controls differ from deciding whether the feature is enabled. Generic lifecycle support could plausibly be templatized but is not evidenced as existing.

Lines 79-108 serialize asynchronous state transitions and recheck desired state after creation. The proposal accurately notes that rejected shutdown leaves stopping true; generic async-resource orchestration could plausibly be produced by reusable tooling.

Lines 69-74 only create/reuse the configuration manager object. Its actual customized behaviors are worker setup, subscription/replay, and conditional settings refresh; this singleton idiom is not a separate customization instance.

Lines 84-102 merge distro/caller profile fields, apply write-once profile filling, and ensure only one background worker is started. The proposal correctly limits distro precedence to the incoming merge; a reusable initialization template is plausible.

Lines 108-112 delegate worker shutdown and empty callbacks; as a manager-level teardown of proposal 22's worker/subscriptions, this adds no separate configuration behavior beyond the worker's actual cancellation in proposal 34.

Lines 119-135 wrap callbacks so duplicate subscriptions can be removed independently and replay nonempty cached settings to late subscribers. This is an independently observable callback integration; a generic callback-cache primitive could plausibly be generated.

The two cited methods isolate callback invocation failures, but these are background configuration subscriber failures, not request retries or custom service error parsing. Other is the more accurate category.

finding.subtype: Isolate synchronous and asynchronous configuration callback failures
finding.explanation: notifyCallbacks visits a copied callback list, while invokeCallback catches synchronous throws and attaches a rejection handler to returned promises, logging either failure without awaiting the callback.
finding.handwrittenRationale: The captured SDK configuration integration contains explicit callback dispatch and failure isolation outside the separately declared generated protocol output; generic subscriber isolation could plausibly be templatized.

decisions.reason: Lines 151-227 and 245-249 implement ETag-based change polling, transient backoff, cached-settings preservation, and conditional update notifications. This retry/error behavior concerns configuration refresh, not ingestion; a conditional-fetch state-machine template is plausibly reusable.

Lines 232-234 expose the cached settings with an object spread; this trivial accessor is an implementation detail of the separately counted settings-refresh behavior, not a distinct SDK customization.

Lines 239-243 explicitly describe and implement a reset intended for test isolation. This is not a separate shipped SDK customization beyond the configuration refresh and worker lifecycle already counted.
Lines 52-57 implement only lazy construction of the profile holder. Its meaningful write-once merge is proposal 30; singleton construction alone adds no independent customization behavior.

Lines 63-70 preserve previously populated profile fields while filling only empty known fields; this write-once precedence affects configuration targeting independently from object creation or snapshot access. The merge shape is reusable.
Lines 75-77 implement a shallow getter for the profile state; this accessor is part of the write-once profile behavior in proposal 30, not a separate customization.
Lines 79-85 identify this reset as primarily for test isolation. It does not add a distinct shipped SDK customization to the write-once profile behavior.

Lines 23-27 and 46-79 implement jittered startup and sequential, abortable polling with bounded reschedule intervals. This is background configuration refresh infrastructure, not an LRO poller, and its scheduling shape is plausibly reusable.

Lines 32-44 actively cancel a pending timer and signal abortion of an in-flight poll. That cancellation is distinct from scheduling and does not claim synchronous termination of the active request; generic worker teardown is plausibly reusable.
